Records the effects of every item: arms, armor, accessories, cures, magic stones and tools. Adventurers get a blank one free; alchemy fills it in.
Given to Doohan adventurers. Magic and alchemy record the abilities of monsters you defeat. Fighting a foe often unlocks deeper analysis.

A greeting from someone met below.

Oda is an orc. A plain no-name orc. Oda lives in town, sees many adventurers - and gets punched by them a lot. Poor Oda! So Oda began this Adventurer Tailing Journal! Read it and learn how pitiful Oda is - and what Karman's maze is like too!

The project starts! Oda scouted for a mark - and found a brand-new adventurer, green as grass. But before Oda moved, Simzon (who always pounded Oda!) got in their face. Bullied on day one? More pitiful than Oda! Decided: Oda tails this one!

Just watching, for now - get caught tailing and Oda gets squashed. The mark made rounds: tavern, temple, inn, guild. Talked with a wild girl, a shady geezer, a temple sister... A party, that mix?! Oda snickered. Pff!
The newcomer headed for Karman's maze - the only famous thing here. Rescue squads keep vanishing inside; find them and the knights let you in. They even got the bracelet. Nobody gives Oda one! Hmph!
The hero got searching. A scream! Oda nearly jumped out of his skin - but it was the lost rescue squad! The hero smashed the monster on them. Knights came running; hero got all the fussing. Envy!

The castle invited the hero in! Sneaky Oda slipped down a secret passage and eavesdropped: the captain talked witch-talk, then - join the Punitive Force! Hero said yes on the spot. Trusting a bit fast, no?

The castle invited the hero in! Oda slipped down a secret passage and listened: witch-talk, then - join the Punitive Force! Our hero paused a while, then said yes. A chewed-on answer is a good answer, right?

Almost forgot the big one! The hero pulled off an Alleid! To Oda that's, uh, nothing much - but doing it without being a mage? Something! Why? The bracelet, that's what's fishy.......! P.S. Reported from Oda's secret passage!

While Oda bound his notes, somebody snatched the journal from behind - one Lidi! Caught! Silenced! ...Wrong! The Boss (Oda's hired now, so: Boss) says tail away and make a great journal, published under Oda's name! The heavens love pitiful Oda!
The real assault on Karman begins! Go, hero! Don't lose! Oda follows anywhere and writes it all! P.S. Oda's debut pen name: reporter PIPIN. Pleased to meetcha!

At the maze door HE showed - Webster! Oda sees him below a lot; he REEKS. He gave the hero a gorgeous reward, then laughed he'd swiped it from the castle! Plenty of baddies aren't monsters. Hero, never bully orcs!

To the hero: nice to meet you! Oda is rookie reporter PIPIN (pen name). The Boss will introduce Oda soon, so Oda's practicing letters. Oda tails real quiet - don't be mad. Happy, shy... Oda's a jumble.
The Boss kept her word! She introduced Oda - and Oda may follow and tail away (sneakily)! Permission! In exchange Oda promised fresh pages, ready any time!
The Boss introduced Oda... but the hero said NO tailing. Sniff. Fine - Oda tails in secret like always. Someday you'll see! Oda keeps the journal stocked and close, for the day you want it!

Hero's doing great - cracked a trick, found the stairs down! But guess who stood there: SIMZON! Orc pals said he'd gone quiet at the temple after something awful below. Why here? The hero just watched.
B2! Dark, damp - Oda's scared. With orc buddies it was fine; alone is different! Brr. If something ate Oda, would the hero notice? Chin up! Tail on!

The missing knights turned up on B2: bound by the statue, all killed. The captain's face was 1000x scarier than ever; Oda nearly cried. But raging, the captain was crying too. Fifteen men at once... next could be Oda. Scary.

Atop B2 sat a device; the hero worked it and fell in a pit. On purpose, right?! Below: Simzon! But wrong, somehow. Oda peeked - BAM! His body burst; out came a creepy THING. Sick to recall. Rest easy, Simzon. The thing? Next page!

The thing sprouted, swelled, bunched - one huge monster! It went for the hero; Oda dove for cover. The hero drove it off! ...Well, it laughed and slid away with plenty left. That mossy thing was a Writhing One. For sure!

Past where it fled: stairs to B3! Below, a gorgeous pyramid - TA-DA! (We were inside it, really.) Oda's plan: paint self white, pass for a King. Camouflage! Hero, if Oda dies, build a tomb this fancy, 'kay?

Wall-scribbles: classic prank (Oda drew himself on a shop wall once. SECRET!). A witch pranks bigger: one blast blew away a chunk of B3 - folk there wiped out! Except one, saved by barfing on B2. Whew: Oda and hero were elsewhere!
Normal folk would quit right there. Not our hero! Through the twisty pyramid, down to B4 - a lava field?! HOT! But in the King getup nobody looks twice. Safe tailing!

On B4 lay Grand Magician Wesbell! The hero revived him - and Aurora appeared, laughed, blinked out! Old friends, those two - they squabbled. She flat ignored the hero. Wesbell can't read her aim, so he trusted the hero with his art. Not bad!

Uri shared worry-talk about Webster (with the hero, not Oda. Hmph). Oda snuck close; nobody noticed. So: Webster and the Grand Temple geezer mean to summon a fancy-named monster - an Apostle! Why? Unknown. But it's Webster: bad news, guaranteed!
Through boiling B4: B5! And there stands the worst guy - Webster! This is Dialant, the legendary elf city. He got here on everyone's backs, and struts like its discoverer! Make him eat it, hero!

One look at THAT and Oda knew: Dialant, for real. A gigantic sword hung from above - the Og, an ancient blade no human today could swing. Webster wants it awake, to destroy the witch. Overdoing it... no?

The hero doesn't stop: B6! Still the maze, but different - solemn, hushed, like something's watching. (Creepy monsters still swarm it.) Oda quit the white paint on B5; plain hide draws less notice. Oda tails from way back.

First time ever, Oda cursed whoever started this gig - that's Oda. B7 is the worst: like living in a huge beast's belly. Squishy walls and floor; trip, and glop smears you. Bleh! But going back alone is scarier. No dying, hero!
Oda hated Webster... but he was a victim too. He made himself the Og's core, life and all. Doom, thought Oda - but the hero laid it to rest! Princess safe, too. Only the witch now.

Free of squishy B7: B8! Deeper is scarier, but ANYTHING beats B7 (air's still nasty though). Truth: Oda underestimated the hero - never dreamed they'd get this deep. And Oda kept up... hold on. Is Oda amazing too?! To the end!

Deeper in, the dead air thickened. Bad feeling - bingo. Before old Langobalt rose a HUGE fiend, moldy like B2's but stronger: a Writhing One! He was gone in a blink; it turned to swallow the hero. And the hero beat even THAT.
After creepy B7-B8: a grand temple quarter?! This fine, this deep. Oda's ready for anything now - could serve the Orc Emperor. (No rank though.)

Just when the stairs felt close - the witch! Aurora seemed to know the hero; a test, maybe. She summoned the mossy B2 thing: SKEDIM!! Grudges are scary - and stronger now! But this time the hero destroyed it. Completely! Yo, champion!
Double digits: floor 10! Like B9 polished shiny - gems stud the walls, sparkle sparkle! Oda's plan: pocket a few for reader presents when the journal's out! Gonna ask the Boss!
The last duel: hero vs Aurora! Oda's cheering worked - the hero WON!! Duhan's champion! Oda: famous orc!

Hero - congrats on beating Aurora! Oda figured you pitiful once; now all Duhan sings your name. Oda's done tailing: what comes next is yours alone. Off to publish this - mega-hit, promise! Later, hero!

First time Oda saw a ghost THAT pretty. Then, shock: no ghost at all - the real Princess Oriana! Hiding in the maze from Webster... like Oda hides from the hero!!! Princess, forget Webster - marry Oda instead?!
For adventurers taking requests. Many jobs carry details too long for the board; clients leave notes, gathered here. Read them and see each job through.
On the altar, a dead band leader. His fellows weep. The priest draws back the face-cloth.
The organ sounds; the priestess sings. Hands over the body, the priest repeats the solemn rite, grave and clear. The fellows close their eyes.
Light wells from the priest's palms into the body. As it wraps him whole, the cold hand warms - and grips back.
He breathes; his eyes open. His fellows' faces swim, blurred by welling tears... --- Perform exactly as scripted. Vital points are in red; learn them by heart.
Care to try the Jankenman crew? Prizes are BIG: 1st Revival Draft; 2nd Shield; 3rd Blessing; 4th Battle; 5th a rare bracelet. Bring the Broken Sword, proof you beat the orc!
* Pixie Fan Club * At: Seraph Shop. For all beaten by - or smitten with - pixies! Gather at Seraph's!
* Succubus Fan Club * At: Seraph Shop. For all who fell to - or for - the succubi! Care to serve them? Gather at Seraph's!

The 6th Trap Contest - a trap-game high-score battle! Splendid prizes. Play during the term; your best score enters, tries unlimited. Past winners: 5th Raiman 86, 4th Ingo 65, 3rd Jin 77, 2nd Lidi 49, 1st Ingo 53.
-- Maze Survey -- Skilled adventurers: past B1's entry stand paired statues; report to the left one. A knights' detail waits. Entries close at term's end. -- The Knights
-- Maze Quiz -- Q1: The knight captain's name? Q2: Duhan's lord? Q3: Statues found on B2? Q4: Trap levers on B3? Q5: Got the sorcerer's earring on B3?

For guides of the Karman Tour. Mind your guests' safety first. The tour covers only the sights of B1-B5; deeper floors are perilous - never take guests below. Descend in order from B1. Enjoy! - Personnel Guild, with Venoan News.
B1: the Grand Balcony. Below yawns the way to B2 - a matchless view. But the bridge hangs so high that visits have grown few.
B2: the Great Spring. A wrought gate guards it; is the spring natural? None can say. No tonic virtue - just delicious. Drink if you pass.
B3: the Hall of Grief. Plain, till Turgot's traders met Aurora's fury. Young Turgot lived; his fellows all fell on the king's deliveries. Pray for them.
B4 is a lava belt, savagely hot - yet here stands a great basin of cold water that never boils. Why? None know. The witch's work? Worth one look.
B5: the Ancient Ward, proven an old-elven city. Why it lies in a maze, scholars only guess. Sure is: elves built it - the sealed ancient weapon Og, close by, is proof.
Soon after this press was founded, an old friend among the knights brought a surprising request: write this guide. I set down only what I checked myself. May it serve you. - Lidi Wallenstein
Ch.1: Duhan's key places / Ch.2: Using camp / Ch.3: Adventuring / Ch.4: Battle / Last: Afterword
Chapter One: Duhan's chief places. Locals may skim; newcomers, walk the town with this in hand.
Seat of Duhan's lord. Common folk may not enter; court business admits a few. Knights watch day and night - do not test them, I am told.
The adventurers' union. Duhan holds many perilous ruins; lest any stray in and be lost, the crown requires guild membership of all who explore.
Of many taverns I name the Luna Light: more than drink, it handles townsfolk's requests with the guild. Short of coin or fame? Look in - and mind your purse in the crowd.
With Jugurtha near, Duhan's alchemist guild is large, drawing mages from all lands. Their trade: fusing monster materials into stones that teach magic. It only looks forbidding; enter boldly.
One inn matters: the Adventurer's Inn. Short of travel lodging, the house renamed itself, cut rates and served adventurers. It thrived; townsfolk use it too.
A priest of doubtful character; wounds healed for donations. For fallen friends, nowhere else.
Shops abound, yet adventurers end at Vigor's: buying, selling, appraisal in one. Orcs loiter there - proper staff; do not report them.
Before the market: a broad fountain square, haunt of couples, handy for meetings. Bazaars appear at times; bargains happen.
A leafy quarter near the center, favored by scholars. Venoan News soon opens here - passing by, bring us your news, please.
The finest quarter: mansions in rows, land dearer than anywhere. Outsiders idling here soon draw the patrols' eyes.
Duhan's roughest ground: drifters and the lawless gather, and toughs pick quarrels. Without business, stay away - and what business would call you there?
All eyes rest on Karman's Labyrinth. Even guild adventurers need the knights' pact to delve. Duhan's other ruins are picked clean; adventure waits there alone.
No adventurer does without camp - yet many misuse it. This chapter treats of camp; veterans too should read with fresh eyes.
Arms, armor, trinkets, stones, physics - all are 'items'. Packs have limits: check stock often, lest you weep at what you discard. Store what merits keeping.
Some spells cast outside battle - Feal, when salves run dry; check your fellows' magic. Attack spells won't cast in town. No Creta on the square.
Poison from traps, curses borne unknowing - strength drains in silence. Watch your party's status always.
Nothing in battle outweighs formation. A swordsman in the rear cannot strike; a frail mage in the van invites death. Set a line that fits your band.
Note every promise taken at the tavern; forget none - a lapsed pledge ends an adventurer's name. Neglect one of mine, and my paper's next page will be all about you.
This chapter walks newcomers through adventure step by step. My way is not the only way: learn the basics, then adventure as you please.
Adventure favors numbers. Alone? At the guild, hire seasoned names or register new fellows - when you want companions, the guild is the door.
Companions found, set your line by class and gift: strikers in front; casters, healers and the frail behind. You shall not rue it.
Line set, HP and MP full - the adventure begins. Its purpose here is one: explore the labyrinth; press into monster country, fight, earn, be honed.
It is a labyrinth because you stray. Fix your road as you go and mind the way home. The guild's map is a marvel: it records by magic each place you walk.
Every labyrinth swarms with monsters - Karman too. Meet one, and life and death begin.
Monster gear is fouled and worn; looks tell little, and curses may hide on purpose. Appraise first: Vigor's, for a fee - or a Bishop, whose gift it is.
Victory earns experience; its store makes your level, the measure of power. But it turns to strength only at the inn. Bank all you like - till your feet carry you there, it counts for naught.
Battle, then. Here are the actions common to every fight - the basics. In the field, weigh the moment; judgment is all.
Each member acts singly, at your command. Read the field; give each a fit order. Every class has its knacks - weigh who does what best.
Strike with your equipped arm - fists, failing that. But arms have reach: close-work blades will not bite from the rear line. And some foes dodge like wind; when steel misses, turn to magic.
HP low? Guard for the turn, and let another restore you meanwhile. Such teamwork carries battles.

Magic is of kinds: attack, restoring, aiding. Learned, the right spell serves nearly any pass; rows do not bind it as they bind steel. But casting costs MP by rank - spend with thought, or need finds you dry.
Items may be used in battle, but the user spends the turn. Keep salves in rear hands, with the supporters: a front line that pauses to drink slays nothing, and the fight circles without end.
Draw the weakened to the rear with a swap. Both swappers lose the turn - yet to keep a needed fellow alive, at times you must.

Struck from behind, your order flips: supporters stand exposed in front, strikers waste in back - and the foe will have his way. First swap the rows whole, re-form your proper line, then press the fight.
No lives suffice for duels past your strength. Foe too strong, party worn? Flee without shame.
Some classes wield arts all their own; this guide will not number them. Take fellows of many classes and try their gifts - some shine outside battle too, and none will fail you.
As orcs live peaceably in town, some creatures below bear no ill will. Cut them down and you coarsen your heart - and just fellows will not love it; the bond takes the wound.
A quick battle is a good one: you read the foe and fought with craft. Fights that drag dull the blade - focus frays, strength ebbs, harm piles on. With hot-headed fellows, take double care.
The guide ends here - a first step, no more. Karman's survey is barely begun; whether its riddle is solved rests with you who read this. Learn something of worth? Send word to Venoan News.

Team arts born when dying adventurers' thoughts lodge in the bracelet. The skilled devise new ones too.
The blue stone set in the bracelet.
Knights' teams that bear hurt or fallen adventurers to the temple; priests tend them.
Vigor's paid club at the annex. Member-only perks. Sign-up: days 1-5 monthly.
Age-old foes of the light, known by many names, risen many times through history.
Relics of old: moving dolls without hearts, built for labor or war.
At Vigor's annex, days 21-25. The ghost Romi reads your hidden talent. Those she names awaken powers they never knew, they say.
Church-state at Venoa's edge; Duhan's foe. Its invasion began Banquo's War.
Issued to every adventurer; worn in the maze. Its blue stone hints at its worth.
Open on maze B1, run by Seraph. Unmanned to keep prices down. Shoplift and die.
Raised by royal order to slay the maze witch. Knights run it with guild volunteers and watched convicts. As free delving is banned, all lawful explorers belong.
Swept all Venoa 20 years ago. A dark memory yet.
The old elves' great arm, 'Og' in their tongue. Scholars hold it survives, sealed away.
Six lands: Duhan, Jugurtha, Haris, Estoria, Sangoht, Gilten.
Famed school-state near Duhan. 'Seek wisdom? Go to Jugurtha.' Shaken when Grand Magician Wesbell left its head seat, it is still Venoa's finest school of magic.
Popo's coinage: born where magic pools past its limit, it drinks in more and swells. Likelier in shut-in places like the maze.
A dread whose hosts waste away in plain sight - hence the name.
The elves' lost age of wonders. Its own weapons, seized by evil, undid it - so it is told.
Ingo's old thief band. Their mark: a cat on cloth left at each job. 99% success. Ingo shone there - he says.
A city of temples; most priests trained there. A land of deep faith.
Stood where Gilten is now; Aurora razed it 300 years ago. A land of mages.
Lidi's small, trusted press. Bestsellers or no, she won't expand: staff = editor Lidi + rookie Pipin. One soul, one orc.
Haris's holy seat; its sway spans every land.
Heaven's envoy for the worthy few. In truth: a monster.
Mercs who raced the Demons of San-Lazare to the depths. Strong, but they spent allies as tools; the town feared them.
Simzon's old merc band; peerless, trusted by the knights, loved by the town.
Ruins older than memory. Its maze came to light when Ortrud broke the seal; most call it old-elven work.
Oriana raised it for the knights' training. Mage-wrought: larger within than without, halls shifting at each entry, warded from outsiders.
Leprechaun shop for cursed gear at B3's scrapyard. The name mocks orcs.
Eats maze corpses. Slow; easy prey.
A thief lost to maze gold. Quick; never fights fair.
A corpse a fiend's hand crept into. Monster now.
Roams the maze hunting men. Weakest of dragons - still a dragon: strong.
Dim, brute-strong. One swing can kill.
Sweet up top; below it charms aid and robs chests.
No pet: a killer cat. Fast, sharp - a rookie's bane.
A lab-fused beast, escaped and bred wild. Flies fast, dodges well, bites - and spits breath.
Zombie kin - but something rides it; it acts with a will.
Giant swarm beetles; some fly at the rear. Plain blades skip off.
Attacks below, drinks in town. A coward: bullies the weak, flees the strong.
Meaner than an orc; crafty and petty. Robs chests - and uses team arts.
A kobold raised undead. Weak - but plain steel can't put it down.
Leaps, flattens, swallows whole - and croaks for friends.
Giant maze spider: spits sticky thread to bind you fast, then closes in with mighty jaws.
Venom-jawed spider; packs spit poison breath together.
An alchemist's cross of two venom spiders: iron-hard, tough, savage. Packs hunt men and monster alike.
A made beast, dog-based. Ugly but bright - some keep them as prized watchdogs.
A dead fiend's soul, unpassed, soured - its touch can poison.
Ever aloft: blades mostly miss it. Its strikes can paralyze - beware.
Nature unknown: a hermit's corpse ridden by wicked will, some say. Mist-like; blows pass through.
Once mountain lords. The maze is theirs; trespassers get crushed.
Sinners' souls, cast off, unpassed. Old malice drives them at the blameless.
Stone given life by demon hands. Half-hearted blows do nothing to it.
A mad alchemist's blend of beasts. Newly made, it ate its maker, fled the lab and bred.
An ogre crossed with worse: dread strength, iron guard. Leads ogre packs.
The bitten rise as vampires in turn; the new-made haunt the maze, waiting on fresh blood.
A dragon slain by men clings to its hate and rises undead. Men name it, and fear it.
Wrapped in spell-fire; its blows melt steel.
Armored in spell-ice; its cold fists freeze even the hardened.
Venom-fleshed; giant might, near every immunity. Thought untouchable - till death magic proved to bite.
Low among demons - still a demon: claw and spell to toy with prey. May call friends to share the sport.
Most feared of fiends, higher rank: blow and spell annihilate all comers without mercy.
Breathes searing fire; its huge fangs pierce - a graze can kill.
It grins as if mocking. Its Long Song steals minds; the sung wander the maze forever.
Slain, it re-forms and outwaits the ages. Trades power for souls, they say. Magic bites it little.
Said to rule fiends, seat unknown. Its true body hides between worlds; only a tenth of it walks Duhan's maze.
Slain by foul power, risen wailing. Its shriek drains who hears it.
Sent from heaven; snared and bound by demon pact. Its song makes even magic slip the mind.
Forsook heaven for demon power; now it gleans men's lives.
A knight's regret risen headless; its storied blade kills at a stroke.
A botched try at the fabled hellhound: a fused horror keeping only hate of men. It roams, finds, devours.
In cursed trance it neither eats nor sleeps - only wanders and fights. Strong, and pitiful.
Bird body, woman's face. Fair once, till the maze twisted her ugly.
A twisted fusion of lizard and elf, they say. Eyeless - the mouths down its body sense you, and strike.
A cleric the dark seduced: cold-lovely, quick, deft in support magic.
Fearsome speed; once human, some say. Tight with fellows - joint strikes come.
A warrior hollowed to a killing thing; rookies die in a pass.
A cleric the dark took: dead-eyed, quiet. It stalks passersby to grant them 'eternal rest'.
Gifted, it chased magic too deep and lost itself. It drifts the maze, a husk that was a mage.
Mind gone, instinct alone swings his blade - the lowest a samurai falls.

Every nature has matches: Maiden pairs best with Maiden, worst with Hot-Blooded. Pairs in a party sway how trust moves - good matches climb quick, bad ones tumble hard. See our nature columns for each!
One make, yet piece differs from piece by the craftsman's hand: weapons in power and bite, armor in guard. A twin of your blade may outdo the one you bear - compare before you sell or toss.

(From Omazo, Masochist.) A Reaper's chill grip is bliss; I let one ride me, as I do. On my camp road, where a wall should stand - an unknown door! In I went; deep inside lay precious gear. Thank my nature!
Some Alleids wake only under set conditions; a nameless tip says class is the key. Test it yourself!

(From Nagul, Belligerent warrior.) B2, hunting coin with an all-warrior crew, an orc mob jumped us. Small fry, but a swarm - so we matched them: all of us swinging as one. Power surged, something incredible. Sixteen orcs, wiped in a blink. Ha!
(From Sniper M.) My gift to you. I am a hunter: what my bow marks, dies. Against strong foes we archers loose as one; pinned by shafts, the beast barely moves, and the front lands blow after blow.

(Trapper Kakeru's tale.) Battles are all surprises - set patterns get you killed. So I tried a change-up: all of us guarding at once. Iron turtle! Physical hits couldn't scratch us. ...When breath and spells came in, though, I truly thought we'd die.

(Magik Society notes.) [Together, stronger.] Last month our six-scholar Team Intelli tried it below: one spell, cast by many in the same breath, worked as if another spell entirely - far stronger. A new door for magic may swing wide.

(Helga's Duhan Dream plan.) Common trade won't make you rich. Test my idea! Name: Magic Sword! ...too plain. THIS: Magic Weapon! Cast a spell ON a weapon - it keeps the power. A dagger turns Ice Dagger! Try it, quick!

(Magik Society notes.) [Anti-Anti-Magic Shell.] The Shell bars our art - our great foe. One counter: cast faster than it rises. Sleepless, we cracked it: many voices, one spell, quicker than the shell can close.

(From Bro. Dispellado.) [Dispel, be praised!] Dispel is wondrous - truly. Our splendid rite: the faithful cast it as one, and whole packs of undead pass on in a breath. Swift rest is mercy! Hasten to the Grateful Dispel Society!

Dec 1. By Ortrud's word we enter Karman's maze. The men crow: a witch? No sword needed. As ever: careless, fearless. Slay Aurora and survivors live like lords. Work worth a life, for those who sell theirs.
Dec 2. Floor 2. No losses; ambushes break on us. Men splash in a fountain as I write. Took a rare light blade - a gift for Vera, who sulks that I left. Survivors: 12.
Dec 3. Floor 3. Two hurt; mood foul. Played by the Queen - these bracelets trap dead men's memories. Skilled work, rotten work. Yet it pays: we learn the fiends' own team arts. Survivors: 12.

Dec 4. Floor 4. First death. My lapse, though against a giant's ambush, light losses. This burning floor recalls rivals roasting a man as bait. I broke them; it scarred me even so. We move on fast. Survivors: 11.

Dec 6. Floor 5, an old elf city. No Aurora; I tire of counting kills. Three died to gargoyles by the great blade. Teams: four and four. The alchemist says wake it and rule Venoa. Fool's talk. Survivors: 8.
Dec 7. Floor 6. A trap took our mage, and with him our magic road home. Back, or on? The men split. Aoi hears MacBain lives; I finished him myself. She leaves to seek the truth. Survivors: 7, 1 away.
Dec 8. Floor 7, like a dead thing's gut. The men wear thin; no jokes now. We should have found her. Tales call Aurora deathless. Why haunt this pit a hundred years? Hiding - or hunting? Survivors: 6.

Dec 10. Floor 8. A song led us to a flooded temple hall - and the witch. 'So Ortrud sends you against the Writhing One.' I drew; she laughed and vanished. A cold, evil air hangs here. Something is close... (It ends here.)
